proved_step: Fixed-advice pattern bound: For every finite set X, every integer s >= 0, and every fixed function D:{0,1}^s x X -> {0,1}, the family of Boolean labelings {x -> D(a,x): a in {0,1}^s} has cardinality at most 2^s. Proof: the map a -> (x -> D(a,x)) has domain {0,1}^s, of cardinality 2^s; the cardinality of its image cannot exceed the cardinality of its domain. Scope: fixed decoder; only the advice varies. This does not imply that a QE reduction's truth-table input is represented by the advice.

proved_step: Corrected decoder lemma: Let X be any finite set, R:X->{0,1}^N any map, L:X->{0,1} any labeling, and C-range any nonempty set of witness circuits. Define D:X x C-range->{0,1} by D(x,C)=L(x). Then D(x,C)=L(x) for every pair (x,C), even when L is nonconstant on fibers of R. Proof: immediate by substitution in the definition of D. Thus condition (b), which permits D to take x as an input, alone does not imply that labels are constant on R-fibers. Scope: this is a logical clarification of condition (b); it does not satisfy the uniformity/resource requirements of the QE* obligation or establish a reduction.

statement: Canonical-witness consequence of universal witness correctness. Let X be a finite set, let A be an oracle, let C_T={C : tt(C^A)=T} be nonempty, and let D:X×C_T→{0,1} satisfy D(x,C)=L(x) for every x∈X and every C∈C_T. For any selected representative C_T^*∈C_T, D(x,C_T^*)=L(x) for all x∈X. Moreover, for every x, the value D(x,C) is constant as C ranges over C_T. Proof: fix x. For any C,C'∈C_T, the assumed correctness gives D(x,C)=L(x)=D(x,C'); selecting C=C_T^* gives the first assertion. Thus universal quantification over witnesses is equivalent, at the level of correctness alone, to correctness for one representative per nonempty truth-table class. This does not bound the cost of finding or evaluating C_T^*, and does not remove x as a decoder input.

statement: Selector-composition lemma. Let X be a finite input set, R:X→Y a reduction map, L:X→{0,1} a labeling, and C_T a nonempty witness set for each relevant T∈Y. Suppose a deterministic selector S(T) outputs some C_T∈C_T, and a deterministic decoder D(x,C) outputs L(x) for every x and every C∈C_{R(x)}. Then A(x)=D(x,S(R(x))) decides L on X. If R, S, and D have running times r, q, and t, respectively, then A runs in time at most r+q+t, plus the time to pass their outputs between procedures. Proof: for any x, put T=R(x). By the selector hypothesis S(T)∈C_T=C_{R(x)}. The universal decoder hypothesis therefore gives D(x,S(R(x)))=L(x). This holds for every x, so A is correct. Scope: this is a conditional composition lemma; it does not establish an efficient selector for the QE* witness sets.
proof: Fix x∈X and let T=R(x). The selector returns C=S(T)∈C_T. Since T=R(x), this is an admissible witness in C_{R(x)}. By the assumed decoder correctness, D(x,C)=L(x). Thus A(x)=L(x) for every x. The stated running-time bound follows by sequentially running R, S, and D and accounting for output handoff.
scope: Finite-domain implication for deterministic procedures with the stated correctness and selector assumptions. No selector construction, QE* reduction, or P≠NP consequence is proved.

proved_step: statement: Finite-family exhaustive selector lemma. Let T be a Boolean truth table of length N, let C_s be a finite family of circuit encodings with |C_s| <= 2^{b(s)}, and let V(T,C) be a deterministic verifier that decides whether tt(C^A)=T in time at most v(N,s) for every C in C_s. If some C in C_s satisfies V(T,C)=1, lexicographic exhaustive search returns a satisfying C in at most 2^{b(s)} verifier calls and time at most 2^{b(s)}v(N,s) plus encoding overhead. Proof: enumerate C_s in lexicographic order, run V on each encoding, and return the first accepting encoding. Finiteness and the assumed existence of an accepting encoding imply termination and correctness. Scope: this gives no QE* resource bound unless 2^{b(s)}v(N,s) fits it, and establishes no reduction or P-versus-NP consequence.

statement: Prefix-extension self-reduction. Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Define E(y,p)=1 iff p extends to a string z with W(y,z). If each E query costs at most q, then for any y with a W-witness, a deterministic selector finds one in at most b queries and O(bq+b) time. Proof: maintain that the current prefix p has a W-witness extension, initially true. Query E(y,p0); append 0 if true, and otherwise append 1. In the latter case a witness extends p by the invariant, and none extends p0, so one extends p1. Thus the invariant persists. After b steps, p is a full-length string and E(y,p)=1 implies W(y,p). This shrinks the exhaustive selector gap to the cost of extension queries; it does not bound that cost for QE* witness sets.

lemma: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and for each relevant y let C_y be nonempty. There exists D:Y×C→{0,1} such that D(R(x),c)=L(x) for every x and every c∈C_{R(x)} iff L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose any c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y with nonempty fiber, set D(y,c) to the common value of L on that fiber; define D arbitrarily on other y. This characterizes the reduction-only interface; it does not show QE* has that interface or an efficient selector.
proved_step: statement: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and let C_y be nonempty for each y in R(X). There exists a decoder D:Y×C→{0,1} satisfying D(R(x),c)=L(x) for all x∈X and c∈C_{R(x)} if and only if L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y∈R(X), define D(y,c) to be the common value of L on R^{-1}(y), independent of c; define D arbitrarily outside R(X). Thus the condition is both necessary and sufficient. It isolates the interface needed for a fiber argument, but does not establish that QE* uses it or that a witness selector is efficient.

proved_step: statement: Adaptive-cost prefix selector. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and suppose an extension-query procedure E(y,p) correctly decides whether p extends to z∈{0,1}^b with W(y,z). If the i-th adaptive query costs at most q_i, then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic selector outputs such a witness using at most b queries and O(b+Σ_{i=1}^b q_i) time. Proof: initialize p=ε, which has a witness extension. For i=1,…,b, query E(y,p0). If true, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. In the latter case, by induction p had a witness extension and no witness extends p0, so some witness extends p1. Thus the invariant that p has a witness extension is preserved. At length b, p itself is a witness. The query count is b and the total cost is O(b+Σq_i). This gives an exact adaptive cost bound but does not bound those query costs for QE* witnesses or close G0001.
